title: Dusen's and Johnson's bands and their halls
summary: The Dusen band played Odd Fellows Hall for rough crowds and Jimmy Palao's Johnson band played Mason's hall for respectable people.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands

blocks.x: Did you ever see Bolden? Yeah. Buddy Bolden? Yeah.
Buddy Bolden, I'll tell you. They had two bands in Al Jays. That was the Doosens Band and the Johnsons Band. Frankie Doosens.

And Buddy Johnson. Now, they have two special halls in Al Jays. They had on Sigwin Street, it was the Oddfellas Hall. They had the Hall on Olivia, on Valette. And Evelyn, the Second Hall of Marys Hall. The Johnson Band. I think you showed us one of those halls buildings. We were up in that section. Yeah. They had a reason for that. Now, I said a leader of the Johnson Band would always play at the Second Hall of Marys Hall. They had a reason for that. He was a leader of the Johnson Band. He was a leader of the Johnson Band. He was a leader of the Johnson Band. The Johnson Band would always play at the Second Hall of Marys Hall. They had a reason for that. Now, I said a leader of the Johnson Band, his name was Jimmy Pollard. And during them days, it's one of the old Creole ladies that raised him. Her name was Miss Spriggs. She was one of the big to-do's of the Second Hall Society. And she got the job, Jimmy was the violinist. She got the job for Jimmy, which was Buddy Johnson's band. See? Well, that's where all the respectable people are. All respectable people. And then, the Oddfellas Hall, my mother rented a single cottage house right next to the Oddfellas Hall. The Oddfellas Hall was on Seguin and Eliza. Frankie Deucin would play there. That's where all the wild people from up in McDonaville, the ratty people, come where they could come in there and kick up. Like that dance once, when they had Peyton, you used to kick for the ham. You heard of Peyton, an old accordion player. Well, they had women and men kicking up for the ham, kicking their legs up. Well, that was all allowed in the Oddfellas Hall.
The ham hanging on the string? Yeah.

You heard of the kick, got it? Sure. They had all kinds of excitements. When the band would make a break and all that. Well, they'd come there with paper bags. Blow the bags up. The band would make a break. Boom! How did the bags go? They have a bar in there? Huh? A bar in there? Oh, sure a bar. What? They had all kinds of stuff in there. All the kinds of wines in the world in there.
